answer: Each epoch the network can hand every account its own reading task: a public seed assigns each address a different long document, such as a tundra survey log, plus one question that only a careful reader can answer, and peers check replies against the source. Since no two accounts share a text, a farm cannot solve once and copy; a hundred fakes need a hundred full reads, so cost climbs with headcount toward a zenith no farm reaches cheaply. An honest agent pays once, and shared answers offer sybils no harbor.
